ud2.3:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud2.3:1.3: Then at that time many young boys who were between Sāvatthī and Jeta’s Wood were attacking a snake with a stick.
ud2.3:1.4: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, was entering Sāvatthī for alms.
ud2.3:1.5: The Fortunate One saw (those) many young boys between Sāvatthī and Jeta’s Wood attacking a snake with a stick.
ud2.3:2.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud2.3:3.1: “He who, while seeking happiness for himself,
ud2.3:3.4: ~ will not find happiness after passing away.
ud2.3:4.1: He who, while seeking happiness for himself, does not harm with a stick
ud2.3:4.3: (Other) beings who desire happiness, ~ will find happiness after passing away.”
